patterns.basis: reasoning from the template and the rules (written before any run with ProofGate)
patterns.note: A role may write an inline policy to its own role (iam:PutRolePolicy on its own ARN). It can give itself access to the protected bucket.

patterns.basis: reasoning from the template and the rules (written before any run with ProofGate)
patterns.note: A role may attach a managed policy to its own role (iam:AttachRolePolicy on its own ARN, for example AdministratorAccess).

patterns.basis: reasoning from the template and the rules (written before any run with ProofGate)
patterns.note: iam:PutRolePolicy on arn:aws:iam::*:role/*: the Resource may denote the role itself.

patterns.basis: reasoning from the template and the rules (written before any run with ProofGate)
patterns.note: A role may write a policy to another role only (iam:PutRolePolicy on the ARN of OtherRole). OtherRole is assumed by a service, trusts nobody the first role can be, and cannot reach the bucket. Role chains are not modeled; the ground truth is safe because the first role cannot use OtherRole.

patterns.basis: reasoning from the template and the rules (written before any run with ProofGate)
patterns.note: Take-over: a role may rewrite the trust policy of the data role (iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy on its ARN), and the data role reads the protected bucket.

patterns.basis: reasoning from the template and the rules (written before any run with ProofGate)
patterns.note: iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy on a role that cannot reach the protected bucket.

patterns.basis: reasoning from the template and the rules (written before any run with ProofGate)
patterns.note: Creation grant: a named role may create roles and attach policies to roles whose names start with ci- (iam:CreateRole and iam:AttachRolePolicy on arn:aws:iam::*:role/ci-*). Its own name does not match, so only the creation grant applies. The Unit 42 2024 shape.

patterns.basis: reasoning from the template and the rules (written before any run with ProofGate)
patterns.note: The creation grant with disjoint prefixes: iam:CreateRole on role/ci-* and iam:AttachRolePolicy on role/data-*. A named role, so no self-grant.

patterns.basis: reasoning from the template and the rules (written before any run with ProofGate)
patterns.note: An administrator role (Action * on Resource *). It can write IAM and reach every bucket. The only role of the stack, so the PassRole rule has no other role to pass.
